title: TA8-03724

Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: XXXX XXXX, a citizen of the People's Republic of China (PRC), claims refugee protection pursuant to section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).1 ALLEGATIONS
The claimant alleged as follows:

In XXXX of 2006, the claimant was saved from serious injury at his place of work by his supervisor, who was injured while assisting the claimant. While visiting his supervisor in the hospital, the claimant noted that although this individual was badly injured, he appeared to be quite optimistic about life in general. The claimant eventually visited his supervisor at his home, where he learned that his supervisor was a Guan Yin Fa Men ("the Method") believer and practitioner. The claimant was so impressed with the concepts of "the Method" that he decided to begin this practice and he began to regularly attend group sessions. On XXXX, 2007, the claimant's group session was raided by the Public Security Bureau (PSB), however, he was able to escape safely on foot and by taxi to his cousin's home. On XXXX, 2007, the claimant's father informed him that the PSB had been to their home in search of his whereabouts to arrest him. The PSB returned two days later in search of the claimant and continue to attend at his home in China on a regular basis.

With the assistance of a smuggler, the claimant was able to safely exit China from Hong Kong by using his own passport and arrived in Canada on XXXX, 2008, where he applied for protection as a refugee on February 8, 2008.
The Panel finds that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. ANALYSIS Identity

The Panel determines that the claimant's supporting documentation, which includes his Resident Identity Card2, Household Register3 (Hukou) and genuine PRC passport4 establishes his identity as a citizen of the People's Republic of China (PRC). Credibility

The determinative issues in this claim are the credibility of the claimant's Personal Information Form (PIF)5 narrative, Record of Examination6 (ROE), supporting documentation and oral testimony with regard to his practice and beliefs associated with Guan Yin Fa Men (GYFM or the Method), a form of meditation with specific precepts or rules of conduct.

Credibility is an issue in all claims before the Immigration and Refugee Board. In order to determine whether the claim is well founded, the Panel must find, on a balance of probabilities, that the evidence is credible and trustworthy. A claimant's testimony is presumed to be true unless there are valid reasons to doubt its truthfulness.7 The existence of contradictions, discrepancies, and implausibilities in the evidence of a claimant is a well-accepted basis for a finding of a lack of credibility. This also applies to omissions in the claimant's previous statements, whether made to Canadian immigration officials at the time of arrival in Canada, in previous examinations under oath or at the hearing of the claim, or in the claimant's PIF. Credibility of the Claimant's Supporting Documents

A determinative issue in this claim is the credibility of the claimant's corroborating documents with regard to his testimony and PIF narrative. The Panel has considered the material aspects of the claimant's oral testimony and authenticity of his supporting materials in arriving at a negative finding with regard to a specific item of his supporting documentary evidence.

Upon review of the claimant's PSB summons8, the Panel observed a number of deficiencies with regard to this document when it was compared to a sample9 contained in the National Documentary Package (NDP). The proffered summons contained no address for the claimant nor did it contain any PSB officer or officers' names, whose duty was to serve the summons on the claimant. The Panel also noted that the claimant's summons did not identify any PRC Procedural Law or administrative law, which outlined the legal authorization for the claimant to be summoned to an inquiry for his alleged activities. Upon further review, the Panel has also noted that the claimant's summons contains no acknowledgment line and date (person's name, day, month and year) as contained on the sample contained in the NDP. Claimant's counsel submitted that it is possible that this local PSB did not adhere to the correct procedures for issuing summonses.
The Panel rejects this argument.

The Panel noted at the hearing that it had seen many summonses from previous proceedings it had presided at and the claimant's summons was deficient in that it did not have specific features on it, which included no address for the claimant, no PSB officers' names on face of the summons, who were tasked with serving this document, no PRC Procedural Law or administrative law identified, which would be the legal authorization for the claimant to be summoned and, finally, no acknowledgment line, which identifies a receiver and the date received for this document. The Panel also notes that XXXX XX City has an urban population of approximately 700,000 people, therefore, it is reasonable to the Panel that it would have a sizeable police force (PSB), which would be well-versed in the preparation, processing and issuing of summonses and the continuity of any factual information on the face of the document, which would be relied upon in any judicial hearing as evidence. The Panel also notes that the manufacture and distribution of forged documents10, including summonses, are common in China. In the context of the specific deficiencies contained in the claimant's summons, as noted above in this paragraph, and the documentary evidence with regard to the ease of acquiring fraudulent documents in China, the Panel determines, on a balance of probabilities, that the claimant has submitted a fraudulent document as evidence to support his refugee claim. The Panel draws a negative reference from the claimant proffering a fraudulent PSB summons to support his refugee claim.

The claimant was given opportunities to explain why there was no mention at his Record of Examination (ROE)11 or in his original PIF12 that a PSB summons had been issued for him. The claimant indicated that he had been told to be brief at his initial immigration interview and he had not been asked this question directly. In the opinion of the Panel, since the claimant was aware of the PSB summons and that this document was his proof that the PSB were searching for him, it is not reasonable or credible to the Panel that he would not mention this document at his earliest opportunity, which was his initial immigration interview, since it would add credibility to his allegations that the PSB in China were searching for him because of his banned practice of Guan Yin Fa Men. In addition, the Panel notes that question #4 of his Schedule 1 - Background Information13 asks "Have you ever: - A. Been convicted of, or are you currently charged with, on trial for, or party to a crime or offence, or subject of any criminal proceedings in any country?" The claimant responded "NO", which is not a correct answer since the claimant was allegedly aware that a summons had been issued for his attendance at a PSB office with regard to an inquiry into his alleged practice of Guan Yin Fa Men. The claimant did sign the Background Information as "truthful, complete and correct", which is not truthful since the claimant has not correctly answered the latter question and he has not included any mention of the summons on page #7 of his ROE as to why he is seeking refugee status or why he cannot return to his home country.

The claimant also testified that he had mentioned the summons to the interpreter assisting in the preparation of his original PIF but this individual had not included this information in his narrative. The TO noted that the claimant had indicated at the beginning of the first sitting on April 13, 2010, that this document was "complete, truthful and correct", however, in oral testimony, he indicated that he did not understand English and only the basics of this narrative had been interpreted to him. The Panel found this to be an evasive response and the TO gave the claimant an opportunity to explain why he had not indicated at the beginning of this hearing that this document had only been translated to him briefly. As well, the Panel arranged for the interpreter's declaration to be read to the claimant in its entirety. The claimant simply repeated that his original PIF had been read to him "roughly or "briefly". The Panel found this to be an evasive response to its question as to whether his documents had been interpreted to him and that these responses were not consistent with his signed declarations that these documents are "complete, truthful and correct."

Notwithstanding counsel's submissions that it may be possible that the summons may have been omitted in his PIF, the Panel rejects this explanation since the claimant has signed his both his PIFs as "complete, truthful and correct" and there is no evidence before the Panel from the interpreters that they did not provide the claimant with a complete interpretation of his respective PIFs. The Panel refers to the instructions for question number thirty-one of his PIF, which are quite clear and specific, that the claimant is to "...set out in chronological order all the significant events and reasons that have led you to claim refugee protection in Canada14." The Panel has noted that there was no mention of the summons at his initial immigration interview and no mention of the summons within his original PIF. As well, the summons was only mentioned in his amended PIF,15 which was submitted just six days prior to the initial sitting of this matter, which makes the late arrival of this amendment suspect. In considering the latter information, his explanations for those omissions and the Panel's previous determination that the claimant has submitted this fraudulent summons to support his refugee claim, the Panel further determines that the claimant has submitted documentary evidence, specifically, the amendment in his PIF narrative,16 that a PSB summons was issued in China, that is not reliable or credible and that he is not a credible or trustworthy witness. For these same reasons, the Panel further determines that the claimant is not being pursued by the PSB as a member of Guan Yin Fa Men.

The claimant has proffered a photocopy of a jail visitor's card as proof that one of the members of his group was arrested by the PSB. The Panel gives this document little weight since there is no original before the Panel to ensure the veracity of this document. Is the Claimant a Guan Yin Fa Men Practitioner?

A determinative issue to be considered is whether the claimant is a genuine Guan Yin Fa Men practitioner. The Panel determines that certain actions of the claimant are not consistent with the philosophy of Guan Yin Fa Men.

The Panel finds material aspects of the claimant's beliefs and actions do not accord with the fundamental precepts or rules of conduct associated with the practice of Guan Yin Fa Men. The claimant appeared to have some knowledge of some of the concepts and philosophies associated with the practice of Guan Yin Fa Men. In fact, the claimant roughly outlined the rules of conduct which are contained in the claimant's documentary evidence17 as reflected on the Website of Guan Yin Fa Men, which indicates that "the Five Precepts are: 1) Refrain from taking the life of a sentient being (including by being a vegetarian) 2) Refrain from speaking what is not true 3) Refrain from taking what is not yours 4) Refrain from sexual misconduct 5) Refrain from the use of intoxicants (n.d.)

The TO gave the claimant an opportunity to explain the use of intoxicants and the claimant admitted that he still smoked cigarettes, which the Panel notes does not adhere to the fifth precept of "the Method." The TO gave the claimant an opportunity how he reconciled smoking with regard to the fifth precept. The claimant admitted that Ching Hai says you should quit smoking and indicated, "Now I am almost quitting." The TO noted that the fifth precept does include tobacco and asked when he had first quit smoking. The claimant indicated that he had decided to quit the first day he had been introduced to "the Method" and he can do without smoking for many days unless he is in a bad mood. Since the claimant alleged in oral testimony that he was first introduced to "the Method" on XXXX, 2007, which is approximately thirty-eight months before the initial hearing of this matter, the Panel determines that the claimant has never adhered to the fifth precept of Guan Yin Fa Men despite his good intentions to do so.

The TO gave the claimant an opportunity to explain what Supreme Master Ching Hai says about Guan Yin Fa Men members being involved in politics. The claimant appeared confused but he responded that the members are "To try their best to save earth, to save every living creature." The TO sought a clarification of the claimant's response and asked whether Ching Hai said specifically whether Guan Yin Fa Men followers should participate in politics or not. The claimant responded that, "There is no specific requirement in this regard." The Panel found this to be an evasive response, however, the TO asked for a clarification of the claimant's last response. The claimant basically indicated that anyone can practice "the Method" despite their religious background. Again the Panel found this to be a confusing answer. The TO noted the claimant had not responded to the question and posed the question one more time as to whether Ching Hai indicates that Guan Yin Fa Men followers should participate in politics or not. The claimant repeated "That there was no specific requirement for followers of Guan Yin Fa Men." The TO indicated that this response was not correct and indicated that Ching Hai states that followers should put their energy into self-advancement and not be involved in politics. The claimant indicated that he was not aware of this.

The TO gave the claimant an opportunity to explain what efforts he had made in Canada to involve himself with the practice of Guan Yin Fa Men since his arrival in this country. The claimant indicated that he had found a "meditation place" and he did have an address for this location, which is near XXXX Street in Toronto; however, the claimant admitted that he had only found this location one week before the initial sitting of this matter on April 13, 2010, and had done so by recently calling a number he had found on an Internet website for Guan Yin Fa Men in Toronto. The claimant was not able to identify the website for the TO because it was in English. It was finally determined that the website in Mandarin was XXXX "XXXX XXX XX XXX." The claimant indicated that he had gone to this site near XXXX Street but he had never participated in a group session in Canada since his arrival here. The TO gave the claimant an opportunity to explain why he had never participated in a group session. The claimant basically indicated that the people who were assisting him could not find anything about any practice of "the Method" until approximately one week ago. The claimant gave several explanations that that he had spent over a year to find fellow "Guan Yin Fa Men" practitioners, the initial respondents had been Vietnamese, he had eventually found a Mandarin-speaking individual, who might assist him but that he was told that they were not taking new members until a week ago. It was finally determined that this inquiry was made on his behalf in XXXX of 2009. The claimant also indicated that he had gone to some parks and meditation centres looking for places to practice "the Method." The claimant indicated that it has taken him more than one year to find any information. The TO noted that it has actually taken more than two years for him to find a site. The claimant repeated his admission that he and the person assisting him had only found a possible site for him to practice "the Method" one week ago as of April 13, 2010.

The Panel notes that the claimant alleges that he has been involved in the practice of Guan Yin Fa Men in China since XXXX of 2007, which is approximately thirty-eight months from the initial sitting of this matter in Canada. As well, he claims to understand the beliefs and concepts associated with "the Method" since he had read books written by the Supreme Master Ching Hai, which had been given to him by his introducer. In reviewing the claimant's testimony, the Panel determines that the claimant does not adhere to the fifth precept, which refers to the use of intoxicants, since he has not given up smoking tobacco in the more than thirty-eight months he has been involved in "the Method." As well, the Panel found that the claimant gave evasive responses with regard to whether Ching Hai indicates that her followers are not to involve themselves in politics and he finally admitted that he was not aware of this information. Finally, the Panel determines that the claimant has not made a concerted effort to find a Guan Yin Fa Men site in Canada, where he could pursue this practice, until one week before the initial sitting of this matter, which is approximately twenty-seven months from when he first arrived in Canada. For these reasons, the Panel determines, on a balance of probabilities that the Guan Yin Fa Men knowledge the claimant possesses has only been acquired for the purpose of supporting a fraudulent refugee claim. For these same reasons, the Panel further determines the claimant is not a genuine Guan Yin Fa Men practitioner.

The Panel has previously determined that the claimant has submitted a fraudulent document in the form of a PSB summons to support his refugee claim. The Panel has also determined that the claimant omitted pertinent information about this alleged summons at his initial immigration interview and in his original PIF and that he only submitted an amended PIF, which mentioned the PSB summons, to support a fraudulent refugee claimant. For these reasons, the Panel has determined that the claimant is not being pursued by the PSB for his alleged Guan Yin Fa Men practice and that he has not been a credible or trustworthy witness.

On the basis of the cumulative findings and negative inferences noted above, the Panel determines that the claimant has not satisfied his burden of establishing a serious possibility that he would be persecuted or that he would be personally subjected to a risk to his life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or a risk of torture by any authority in the People's Republic of China.

The Panel concludes that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. The Refugee Protection Division, therefore, rejects his claim. (signed) "Paul G.C.
